title: Bimanual Interference Experimental Paradigm
author: Rini Varghese
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7r3hm8n
materials: to the mid-upper right arm FIGURE

steps.title: Set up room and equipment
steps.instruction: Place the 60‑inch flat‑screen HD display on the glass tabletop, mount the mirror 35 cm above the table surface, and position the two air‑sleds (one per limb) beneath the mirror. Connect the TrakSTAR electromagnetic tracking box, the air‑sled compressor, the HDTV, and the iMac running Kinereach software. Verify that the mirror blocks direct vision of the arms and hands.

steps.title: Adjust chair and harnesses
steps.instruction: Seat the participant in the adjustable chair facing the table. Secure a horizontal harness across the waist and a vertical harness around each shoulder. Use the chair‑height lever so the mirror is at the participant’s chin level, then push the chair inward until both arms can rest at shoulder height on the table; lock the chair. Ensure the participant’s legs do not interfere with the transmitter under the table and place their feet on a small wooden step stool.

steps.title: Verify visual display
steps.instruction: Ask the participant, “Are you able to see most of the screen?” and confirm that the target display is clearly visible through the mirror.

steps.title: Attach electromagnetic sensors
steps.instruction: Secure four Ascension TrakSTAR sensors with adhesive tape and a soft pre‑wrap:

substeps.instruction: Sensor 1: dorsum of the left hand on the second metacarpal (as close in line to the middle finger as possible).
Sensor 2: mid‑upper left arm.
Sensor 3: dorsum of the right hand on the second metacarpal (as close in line to the middle finger as possible).
Sensor 4: mid‑upper right arm.

steps.title: Perform safety check
steps.instruction: Confirm the participant has no metal implants or pacemakers. Route sensor wires along the arms to avoid tangles. Ensure the pre‑wrap is snug but not so tight as to impede circulation; ask the participant and re‑wrap if necessary.

steps.title: Calibrate sensors and digitize landmarks
steps.instruction: With the participant remaining still, run the Kinereach calibration routine:

substeps.instruction: Place the reference sensor (Sensor 2) on the prescribed anatomical landmarks in the order specified by the software (left arm first, then right arm).
Check that the elbow is at ~90° and the upper arm is at ~0° (neutral). Adjust if needed.

steps.title: Configure air‑sled system
steps.instruction: Turn on the air‑sled compressor, set the pressure to 13 psi (adjust if device‑specific), and verify airflow is on and even for both sleds.

substeps.instruction: Instruct the participant to rest the thumb in the sled groove and align the forearm with the sled.
Secure each arm with the Velcro straps, ensuring the air tube remains unobstructed.
Set the initial joint angles: elbow flexion 70‑80°, shoulder horizontal abduction 20‑30°.
Position the start circles 25 cm from the table edge and 24 cm apart.

steps.title: Power on all devices
steps.instruction: Turn on the HDTV, flip the power switch on the TrakSTAR box (located on the back), and start the iMac computer with Kinereach software.

steps.title: Program task parameters in Kinereach
steps.instruction: Enter the following fixed (f) and variable (v) parameters:

substeps.instruction: Start circle: diameter = 1 cm, color = green.
Concentric target circle: diameter = 3 cm, color = [as defined in Figure 5].
Number of targets: 1 or 2 depending on experimental condition.
Visual cursor (first proximal interphalangeal joint): diameter = 1 cm, color = black crosshair, update rate = 1 Hz (condition‑dependent).
Hold cursor within start circle for 500 ms.
Go‑tone delay (target foreperiod): random 350–500 ms.
Trial maximum duration: 5 s.
Movement‑end criterion: hand velocity ≤ 0.02 m/s (computed in real time).
Feedback display duration: 1 s after movement end.
Knowledge of Results (KR) grading: 10 points for center, 3 points for second concentric ring (diameter × 2), 1 point for third concentric ring (diameter × 3).
Knowledge of Performance (KP): show a red dot at the veridical cursor position at movement end.

steps.title: Run experimental trials
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant: “After the beep, move as quickly and accurately as you can to the target. Stop at the target.” Emphasize speed and accuracy, not inter‑limb synchrony. Conduct 20 rapid reaches per condition (unimanual left, unimanual right, bimanual left‑right, bimanual right‑left) for a total of 80 trials, excluding practice trials. Provide verbal reminders to be quick and accurate approximately every 5–10 trials.

steps.title: Provide feedback after each trial
steps.instruction: At movement end (velocity ≤ 0.02 m/s), display KR and KP feedback for 1 s as programmed. Verbal encouragement (“Try to go faster”) may be given, especially for stroke survivors who tend to slow down.
